# External scam-message datasets

These are sourced CSV copies with obvious email addresses, phone-like contact
numbers and literal URLs redacted to generic markers. The upstream attribution
and known limitations are recorded here. `scripts/train_expanded_model.py`
maps labels and further normalizes identifiers for model input. The original
`data/back.dataset.csv` remains unchanged.

## Indian scam/ham corpus

- Source: [anmolshrivastav/scam-ham-india](https://huggingface.co/datasets/anmolshrivastav/scam-ham-india)
- File: `anmolshrivastav_scam-ham-india.csv`
- Dataset card reports 2,272 English Indian SMS/message examples, 1,377 ham and
  895 scam/spam, under Apache-2.0. It describes the corpus as a mixture of
  real-world messages and augmented synthetic examples. The CSV has no
  per-row provenance, so this mixture cannot be separated or independently
  audited; it is used as training data only, never as the held-out test set.

## Financial scams detection corpus

- Citation: Ahmed, Al Rafi; Islam, Gazi Faizul (2025), “Financial scams
  detection dataset”, Mendeley Data, V2, DOI
  [10.17632/znsk27yk3h.2](https://doi.org/10.17632/znsk27yk3h.2).
- File: `mendeley_financial_scams_v2.csv`
- License: CC BY 4.0. The dataset card describes manually labeled scam/ham
  messages collected with consent and anonymized, covering English and Bangla.
- The downloaded file contains 523 rows (310 scam, 213 ham), three repeated
  rows, and one normalized template group with conflicting labels. Training
  removes exact duplicate rows and excludes the conflicting group. The
  remaining template groups provide validation and held-out test data.

## Task caveat

Both sources are scam-message corpora (SMS/chat), not a representative corpus
of financial advertisements. They can broaden scam vocabulary, but reported
metrics on these messages do not establish accuracy on real financial ads.
The original `data/back.dataset.csv` is retained and used as additional
training data. No examples are generated by TRACE//FIN.
